mapping.state: 0 or 700 nA per physical cell; a bit is a pseudodifferential pair (700,0) or (0,700)
mapping.adc_kind: differential; one converter per cell pair output, 128 total
mapping.encoding_note: Two complementary branch-selection bits per bit; 700 nA magnitude hardwired locally. Logical INT8 signed two complement is reconstructed digitally.

write.target: both branch states settled; release complete after common control
write.verify_note: GC-04 uses current feedback/self-calibration during fine write, not a separate read/verify loop; 65 ns measured transfer settling is not all-cell BER certification
write.load_isolation: Disconnect added integration/SAR sampling capacitance during programming using local switches; source 65 ns write anchor assumes approximately original 50 fF BL load including switch parasitics. Reconnect/settle is included in dedicated read slot; if write load increases, 65 ns must be revalidated/rebudgeted.
write.fixed_scenario_resources: 128pair drivers/256branches,128diffADCs and128sign decoders fixed acrossshort/reference/long;700nAendpoint target per pair;coarse voltage stage coversfixed50fFprogram load inshort5ns;additional integration/SAR load isolated

refresh.policy: Fixed400us round-robin read/sign-decode/rewrite overone native64x64INT8matrix;all selectedADC,localcodebus andwrite drivers reserved;one128-bit refresh code buffer only;no full-matrix shadow and no assumed demand-write refresh credit
refresh.reader: same differential ADC frontend, one row at a time; 128 bits decoded to 256 branch controls per group
refresh.reliability: 0.4 ms source: 99.7% tested +/-7 cells drift <1 source ADC LSB, not all-bit-error-free. Binary endpoint threshold at zero gives materially wider margin than MLC nearest-level rounding; tail, noise, repeated-refresh stability remain validation conditions.
refresh.sign_decode: One local binary sign decoder per differential ADC, 128 in main or 256 in wide32; one TD parallel decode, independent of 16 MVM reconstruction lanes.
refresh.phase_control: Before each fixed refresh start inhibit new batches for maximum nonpreemptive group length G; fixed order and fixed start ensure per-cell writeback period <=400 us. G is charged once per period. Establish phase after cold initialization; metrics are steady-state intervals, not first-load latency.

frontend_selection.anchor: GC-04 PDF pp6-7 Fig10: measured 180 ns whole compute includes precharge, DTC/MAC and 5b SAR. This anchors only the overall scale; it does not identify individual stages in the adapted frontend.
frontend_selection.conditions: Retain native 64-cell bitline load, 700 nA endpoint, 200 fF effective integration capacitance per branch and +/-224 mV differential range. MAC 1 ns and single-pair refresh 64 ns are engineering integration choices. The main fixed controller allocates a common 64 ns integration window plus 36/86/136 ns aggregate precharge/select/settle/sample/recovery allowance, then shared TI and TA. MAC does not require 64 ns integration: its remaining 63 ns is controller reservation. The early_release comparison removes that reservation only if the same common allowance covers the actual mode and sampling can start immediately after the configured pulse. Neither phase allowance nor early release is independently measured. Writing isolates added integration/SAR capacitance and retains approximately original 50 fF program load.

phase_evidence.confirmed: Distinct precharge, variable-RWL MAC and sampled SAR phases; single-row retention reads tune RWL pulse to ADC range. The source reports no separated adapted 1/64 ns phase budget.
phase_evidence.common_physical_conditions: Same selected 64-cell local bitline, effective integration load, endpoint current, full-scale range and ADC; different number of active rows and RWL width. Equal worst-case integrated charge does not prove equal settling/noise.
phase_evidence.assumed_common_stages: Aggregate precharge, selection, load reconnect/settle, sample and recovery; no unsupported numerical subdivision of the 36/86/136 ns allowance.
phase_evidence.qualification: Early release needs mode-specific timing closure with the same load and settling endpoint. This is an operation/control comparison, not a faster measured GC device.

precision.compute: calibrated approximate ACIM; binary stored weights are sign-decoded during maintenance
precision.sum: 64 endpoint signs -> -64..64, 129 levels; recover binary sum (differential normalized sum + input popcount)/2; digital two ticks must cover this correction and plane/input reconstruction
precision.not_claimed: No DCIM exactness or universal error threshold; no all-cell retention certification

structural_comparison.note: Double true differential ADC and write-pair drivers, retain 16 digital output lanes, same physical state and capacity; frontend budget conditioned to remain 175 ns at equal 64-cell local load

exceptions.source: GC-04 pp.6-7 Fig.10; same native BL load; one row group for K=64, two row groups only in the K=128 capacity contrast

exceptions.selected: two pseudodifferential 3T1C cells per bit at opposite endpoint currents
exceptions.source: GC-04 p6 Fig8; endpoint-only choice; adds actual cells and branch controls, no payload duplication

exceptions.selected: Retained. Source full 180 ns is used only as a scale anchor and is not added as a fourth stage. Shared TA genuinely propagates.
exceptions.source: GC-04 pp6-7 180 ns full cycle uses 5b ADC; our dedicated budget and 10b SAR adaptation are explicitly engineering choices.

fixed_slot.release_rule: Both modes sample/convert after the same reserved integration window; the MAC pulse stops after 1 ns and holds its analog result during the remaining reservation. The 63 ns is a control allocation, not required integration.
fixed_slot.condition: Hold droop, leakage and common-mode settling must remain within the stated approximate-ACIM service during the reserved window.

early_release.release_rule: Sample/convert after each mode pulse: 1 ns MAC, 64 ns single-pair refresh. No full-matrix shadow or extra ADC/driver is introduced.
early_release.condition: Control supports mode-specific release and aggregate common stages retain their allocated 36/86/136 ns at the same bias, load, range and settling endpoint. The original 180 ns cycle alone does not establish this.
